frase_inicial: Daniel and Emily: protecting your family and your future is tugging on the same yearly savings.

tarjetas.frente: The safety net is thin for two earners and two kids
tarjetas.reverso: If a paycheck stops, your bank cash only covers a month of essentials and the near-term vacation would shrink that cushion. That makes you likely to rely on high-cost credit or pause other plans.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash $19,000 today; recommended reserve 8–9 months ($106,860–$120,218); shortfall to adjusted min including vacation $92,360.

tarjetas.frente: Life cover and liability protection are much lower than the family needs
tarjetas.reverso: With two incomes at risk and a mortgage, the current life and no umbrella would leave the remaining earner and the kids exposed. Raising protection reduces the chance that a single event drains your savings.
tarjetas.detalle: Daniel life $250,000 (shortfall ~$1,350,000); Emily life $200,000 (shortfall ~$1,000,000); no umbrella (recommended $1,000,000).

tarjetas.frente: Retirement is the biggest long-term gap but it competes with nearer needs
tarjetas.reverso: Nothing is going into either workplace retirement plan today, so closing the shortfall would need far more yearly saving than you currently have free. That means you must choose which near-term goals share your cash flow.
tarjetas.detalle: Required extra retirement saving about $34,165/yr; net cash flow today $15,032/yr; projected retirement need ~$124,071/yr with guaranteed income covering 49%.

tarjetas.frente: College is funded partly but still leaves a clear gap
tarjetas.reverso: You are already saving to the college plan each year, which helps, yet a funding gap remains so you’ll either add a bit more to the college account or accept more borrowing later.
tarjetas.detalle: 529 balance $30,000; current 529 contributions $8,000/yr; remaining college funding gap ~$106,552 across both kids.

tarjetas.frente: The high-rate credit card is costing you most each month
tarjetas.reverso: At the current payment the balance will take years to clear and interest is the expensive part of your monthly outflows. Paying a bit extra speeds relief without touching retirement or college choices right away.
tarjetas.detalle: Card balance $18,000 at 24.9%; monthly payment $450; interest portion currently about $373.50/month.

movimientos.title: Raise mortality coverage
movimientos.action: Add $1,166,000 of life cover to reach the next mortality-coverage anchor

movimientos.title: Add umbrella cover
movimientos.action: Add $1M of umbrella to raise the liability shield

movimientos.title: Raise annual savings
movimientos.action: Redirect $15,032/year of free cash flow into savings to raise retirement-directed savings toward the next band

siguiente_paso.razon: Protection gaps are the weakest part of your plan and matter most to the kids and to the household if an income stops. The plan flags adding life cover as a low-effort move that raises your overall score and gives both of you clearer leeway with the same free cash flow.
pasos: Sit down together with recent life policy statements and employer benefits
Call or email each employer benefits team to confirm any existing life cover and whether extra group cover is available
If employer information is unclear, schedule a short call with a local adviser to get quotes for adding individual life and an umbrella policy
